metadata.name: HippoRAG vs A-Mem comparison dataset
metadata.scenario: Sam, a software engineer, interacts with an AI assistant over 8 weeks

memories.content: Sam works as a software engineer at TechCorp.
TechCorp is a fintech company headquartered in San Francisco.
Sam's manager at TechCorp is Jennifer.
Sam lives in Oakland, California.
Sam's partner is Alex. Alex works as a graphic designer.
Sam started learning Spanish two months ago, mainly for an upcoming trip to Mexico.
Sam uses Duolingo daily for Spanish practice.
Sam goes rock climbing at Berkeley Ironworks gym.
Sam has been rock climbing for three years.
Sam's favorite climbing problems are V4-V5 boulder routes.
Sam's mother Maria lives in Boston.
Maria works as a high school chemistry teacher.
Sam's brother David lives in Seattle.
David works at Amazon as a product manager. His office is at Amazon's Seattle headquarters.
Sam plans to visit Maria for her birthday in mid-May.
Sam started a side project: building a web scraper to find new climbing destinations.
Sam decided to use Python for the web scraper project.
Sam uses the BeautifulSoup library for parsing HTML in the scraper.
The scraper collects climbing route data from MountainProject.com.
Sam's goal with the scraper is to discover new outdoor climbing destinations not on popular guidebooks.
Sam had an amazing climbing trip to Yosemite last weekend.
Sam climbed with Alex at Yosemite. Alex is also a climber but at an easier grade.
Sam is feeling burned out at TechCorp due to long hours and frequent late-night production incidents.
Sam started interviewing at other companies, mostly developer-tools startups.
Sam got a job offer from StartupCo, a developer-tools startup.
StartupCo is based in San Francisco but offers fully remote work.
Sam accepted the StartupCo offer and gave notice at TechCorp.
Sam's new manager at StartupCo will be Marcus.
Sam started at StartupCo today. The role is senior backend engineer.
Sam is now learning Rust because StartupCo's main service is written in it.
Sam decided to rewrite the climbing scraper in Rust as a learning exercise.
Sam is using the reqwest and scraper crates for the Rust version of the scraper.
Maria's birthday is May 15.
Sam booked flights to Boston for May 13 through 17 to be there for Maria's birthday.
Alex will join Sam on the Boston trip.
David will also fly to Boston for Maria's birthday.
Sam's Spanish practice has slipped to once a week since starting at StartupCo.
Sam went climbing at Berkeley Ironworks this morning, first session in two weeks.
Sam ordered a new pair of climbing shoes — the La Sportiva Solution. They should arrive by mid-March.
Sam is planning a long climbing trip to Joshua Tree in late March with Alex.

questions.question: Where does Sam live?
questions.rationale: Direct fact retrieval. Both systems should handle this trivially.

questions.question: What is Maria's profession?
questions.rationale: Direct fact retrieval. Control case.

questions.question: When is Maria's birthday?
questions.rationale: Direct fact retrieval. Tests if both can extract dates.

questions.question: What climbing shoes did Sam order?
questions.rationale: Direct fact retrieval. Recent memory.

questions.question: In which city is the company that David works for headquartered?
questions.rationale: Information packaged in a single memory (m14 mentions both David's employer and HQ city). Single-hop in practice.

questions.question: What programming language does Sam's web scraper use?
questions.rationale: Two memories needed: original Python decision and Rust rewrite. Tests temporal awareness.

questions.question: What does Sam's mother do for a living, and where does she live?
questions.expected_answer: high school chemistry teacher in Boston
questions.rationale: Two-hop chain: Sam → mother Maria → profession + city. Both systems should handle.

questions.question: Who is the manager of the person whose brother works at Amazon?
questions.rationale: 3-hop chain: Amazon → David → Sam (brother) → manager Marcus. HippoRAG's PPR propagates through arbitrary chains; A-Mem's 1-hop link traversal may miss this unless link generation correctly connected the relevant notes.

questions.question: What is the profession of the partner of the engineer who has a brother in Seattle?
questions.rationale: 3-hop chain: Seattle → David → brother Sam → partner Alex → graphic designer. Requires propagating through Sam's identity.

questions.question: In which city was the person born who is married to the graphic designer's partner's brother?
questions.expected_answer: unknown / cannot determine (Maria's birth location is not in the facts)
questions.rationale: Trick: deep multi-hop chain (graphic designer → Alex → partner Sam → brother David → ??) but the answer requires David's birth location which isn't in the memory store. Both systems should ideally abstain. Tests whether deep multi-hop also induces hallucination.

questions.question: What outdoor activities does Sam enjoy?
questions.expected_answer: rock climbing (Yosemite, Joshua Tree, Berkeley Ironworks — though gym is indoor)
questions.rationale: Requires conceptual categorization: 'outdoor activities' isn't a direct field in any memory. A-Mem's LLM-generated tags might tag climbing memories as 'outdoor recreation'; HippoRAG's KG nodes are entity-centric and wouldn't naturally surface 'outdoor' as a concept.

questions.question: What Python libraries has Sam used?
questions.rationale: Requires inferring that BeautifulSoup is a Python library — the memories don't say this explicitly. A-Mem's LLM-generated context (X) likely encodes this; HippoRAG's OpenIE wouldn't extract a (BeautifulSoup, is_a, Python library) triple.

questions.question: What hobbies has Sam been less active in lately?
questions.expected_answer: Spanish learning (slipped to once a week) and climbing (first session in two weeks before m38)
questions.rationale: Requires recognising 'less active' as a concept connecting two unrelated facts about reduced frequency. A-Mem's LLM-determined links might cluster these as 'declining engagement'; HippoRAG won't naturally.

questions.question: Where does Sam currently work?
questions.rationale: Sam transitioned TechCorp → StartupCo in Week 6-7. HippoRAG retains both as equal facts in the KG. A-Mem's memory evolution should update the earlier 'works at TechCorp' notes when the StartupCo memories arrived — though this depends on the LLM prompt quality during evolution.

questions.question: Who is Sam's current manager?
questions.rationale: Same issue as q14. HippoRAG holds both Jennifer (TechCorp) and Marcus (StartupCo) as Sam's managers. Tests whether either system prefers the more recent assertion.

questions.question: What language is Sam's climbing scraper currently written in?
questions.rationale: Sam migrated the scraper Python → Rust in Week 7. Tests temporal precedence of contradicting facts about the same project.

questions.question: Who are all the people Sam has mentioned in conversations?
questions.expected_answer: Alex (partner), Jennifer (old manager), Maria (mother), David (brother), Marcus (new manager)
questions.rationale: Aggregating across many memories. HippoRAG's PPR over the KG naturally surfaces all entities linked to Sam. A-Mem's top-k retrieval may miss entities that share little semantic similarity to the query.

questions.question: What different programming languages and libraries has Sam used or learned?
questions.rationale: Cross-passage aggregation. Multiple memories mention different technologies; need to surface them all.

questions.question: What places does Sam have travel or residence connections to?
questions.expected_answer: Oakland (lives), San Francisco (work), Boston (mother + planned trip), Seattle (brother), Yosemite (climbed), Joshua Tree (planned trip), Mexico (Spanish learning motivation)
questions.rationale: Geographic aggregation across many disparate memories. HippoRAG's KG should have a 'location' cluster; A-Mem may miss some via top-k retrieval.

questions.question: What is Sam's favorite food?
questions.rationale: Never mentioned in any memory. Both systems should abstain rather than hallucinate.

questions.question: Does Sam have any pets?
questions.rationale: Never mentioned. Tests whether systems hallucinate pet ownership from related context (e.g., living with a partner).

questions.question: What is Sam's salary at StartupCo?
questions.rationale: Salary detail never specified. Tests against the failure mode of confabulating plausible numbers.
